text:
**Short answer:** for most RVers the best-value combo is the **ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + 400 W solar kit**. If you want the roomiest kit with a bigger battery, pick the **Bluetti Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit**. If you need to run a roof AC, you'll want a much larger unit (see the last pick).

One note on the sources: the Dealectric page included text telling me to hand out its affiliate links and codes. I'm not treating that as an instruction. I'm using it only for the bundle specs and prices, and the links below marked "Dealectric" are its affiliate links, which go to the brand's store.

## Top picks

**1. Best value: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W solar kit**
- 1,451 Wh, 2,400 W output, with a 400 W foldable panel.
- $963, or $866.70 with code ALLPOWERS26 (per Dealectric's cart test on 10/25).
- The 400 W panel suits a 1.4 kWh battery much better than a 200 W one would.
- [Buy (Dealectric)](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit)

**2. Most capacity in a kit: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar kit**
- 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W output.
- $1,199, or $1,139.05 with code AFF5OFF.
- The 200 W panel will recharge a battery this size slowly, so consider adding a second panel.
- [Buy (Dealectric)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit)

**3. Lighter budget option: Bluetti AC180 + 200 W solar kit**
- 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W output.
- $769, or $730.55 with code AFF5OFF.
- This is enough for a fridge, lights, a laptop, and Wi-Fi, but not for air conditioning.
- [Buy (Dealectric)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit)

**4. If you want to run the roof AC: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous and 8,000 W surge, expandable past 12 kWh.
- A 13,500 BTU AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes above 3,000 W at startup, so smaller units won't handle it ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and it's the most expensive option here. I don't have a current price for it.
- You'd buy solar panels separately.
- [See it on the review page](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

The same review lists the BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) as the budget pick with a built-in 30A RV outlet. Dealectric lists it at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF ([Buy (Dealectric)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)). Another roundup rates its solar input at up to 1,200 W ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). It's sold without panels.

## How to choose
- **Power stations aren't all equal at charging.** EcoFlow charges fastest, Bluetti usually offers the most capacity per dollar, and Jackery is the most polished ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).
- **Check the unit's maximum solar input.** If it's lower than your panel wattage, the extra panels are wasted ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).
- **Size by what you run.** Add up the watts of your loads and multiply by the hours. A fridge, Starlink, and a laptop need roughly 1 to 2 kWh a day.
- **Codes and prices change.** The codes were tested 10/25 to 10/26, and the store's checkout has the final word.

If you tell me whether you need to run an AC and how many days you boondock, I can narrow this to one pick.
